newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to raise $150 million in samurai issue.
newsitem.headline: Israel to raise $150 million in samurai issue.

text.p: Israel will raise $150 million in the Japanese market for the first time ever sometime toward the end of the first half, the Treasury said on Monday.

The Treasury also said it intends to return to the Yankee market to raise another $200 million later this year. It said the timing of the Yankee issue would depend on the extent of Israel's foreign currency debt in relation to gross domestic product and the country's foreign currency requirements.

Underwriters for the Samurai issue, which will be equal to about 20 billion yen, will be chosen at the end of the month when a Treasury delegation headed by director-general David Brodet visits Japan.
Accountant-general Shai Talomon said the Treasury intends to borrow $2.6 billion in foreign currency from various sources this year.
This will include $1.265 billion raised as part of the U.S. loan-guarantee programme, $900 million via Israel Bonds and the rest through issues, like the Samurai offering, made without U.S. backing.
Israel raised $750 million at the start of January in the U.S. loan-guarantee programme, which expires in October 1998.

The independent offerings are part of a strategic programme begun in 1995 aimed at exposing Israel to the world financial markets and diversify its sources of foreign currency borrowing ahead of the expiry of the U.S. guarantees programme.
"These independent offerings will create flexibility in determining funding sources by maturity, currency and other terms," the Treasury said.
As part of the programme, Israel made a $250 million Yankee issue in 1995 and a $200 million Eurobond issue last December.

The Treasury said a Moody's delegation is now in Israel to complete their annual update of Israel's credit rating. Moody's will also provide a rating for the Samurai bonds close to the offering date, the Treasury added.
